episodes.title: Out of Touch
episodes.summary: Dr. Leo A. Gordon’s essay on the vanishing sense of touch in modern surgery, from the “tissue sense” of open operations to laparoscopy and robotic consoles.
episodes.description:
Out of Touch — The Vanishing Sense of Touch in Modern Surgery.

In this episode, we explore Dr. Leo A. Gordon’s reflective essay, “Out of Touch,” which examines how rapid technological advances have transformed general surgery and altered the physician–patient relationship. Dr. Gordon recounts his early career choices, driven by the desire to directly touch and cradle human pathology in his hands to relieve suffering. He explains how years of practice cultivate “tissue sense”—a surgeon’s refined ability to evaluate inflammation and gauge tissue condition through direct tactile contact.

The discussion traces the evolution from traditional open surgery to minimally invasive procedures. With the introduction of laparoscopy, surgeons exchanged direct physical contact for light sticks and video monitors, turning intimate operations into experiences separated by a thick glass partition. The episode further explores the transition to robotic surgery, where practitioners operate from distant consoles, and concludes with a speculative look at the future of medical progress.
